Joining opens the study consent form. The app needs no account and sends no device ID. It stores study access, drafts and unconfirmed answers on this device. What the questions collect is explained in the study consent. A study cannot see your other studies.

This phone stores the study list, schedules and access keys, temporary drafts, cached questionnaires, answers awaiting confirmation and transfer receipts. The app needs no account and sends no device ID. These local study data are excluded from backups and device transfers. For each study it also keeps whether its notifications ring with a sound, and the labels of shortcuts you put on your home screen are kept by your home screen.

For studies that allow offline answers, the app also keeps questionnaire pages. Offline answers remain encrypted on this phone until the server confirms storage or you explicitly discard them or remove the study. Expiry or refusal does not delete them.

The questionnaires open in Android System WebView, a part of the phone that comes from Google. Depending on the phone\'s settings, WebView may contact Google services itself, for example Safe Browsing, which checks addresses against lists of harmful sites, or suggestions for filling in forms. The app has switched off WebView\'s usage statistics and does not offer the answers to any autofill service.
Quiet hours for short surveys at random times: %1$s
No short survey at a random time comes during your quiet hours. A change applies from tomorrow and only to the short surveys at random times, not to those at fixed times.
If you set quiet hours for a study, the app keeps them and sends them to the server of the study, so that no short survey at a random time comes during them.

Some phones stop apps in the background to save battery; short surveys then arrive late or not at all. In the list “Battery optimisation”, set Askurious to “Don’t optimise”. On some phones the setting is in the app info under “Battery”.
